companies.name: Teradyne, Inc.

margins.trend_note: GAAP operating margin exploded to 32.9% from 13.9% a year ago as AI/HBM-driven semiconductor test demand roughly doubled revenue on a largely fixed cost base.

fcf.note: TTM FCF ~$800M (H1 2026 alone was ~$579M vs ~$229M in H1 2025), inflecting sharply upward with the revenue surge.

balance_sheet.note: Cash plus marketable securities of ~$517M against essentially no borrowings (only ~$100M of lease liabilities); clean net-cash balance sheet.

segments.name: Semiconductor Test
segments.note: $1,122M in Q2 2026, the overwhelming growth driver on AI compute and HBM/memory test demand (segment YoY not separately verified).

segments.name: Robotics
segments.note: $100M in Q2 2026; still a small, slower-growing piece (Universal Robots/MiR).

companies.guidance_note: Q3 2026 guided to $1.20-1.30B revenue and GAAP EPS $1.79-2.09, roughly flat sequentially but up ~60%+ YoY at midpoint.
companies.execution_note: Multiple consecutive record quarters with results at/above guidance (Q2 revenue $1.329B, GAAP EPS $2.38 vs $0.49 a year ago); strong beat pattern through the AI upcycle.

moat.note: Effective duopoly with Advantest in semiconductor ATE with deep design-in switching costs at leading-edge compute/memory customers; cyclical but structurally entrenched.

risks: Extreme cyclicality - revenue doubled YoY and can reverse hard if AI capex digests
Customer concentration in a handful of leading-edge compute/HBM customers
Robotics segment remains subscale and weak
China/export-control exposure

thesis_fit.note: Teradyne is a direct toll-taker on the AI compute exponential: every leading-edge accelerator and HBM stack must be tested, and rising device complexity increases test intensity per chip. The exponential is the core business (semi test is ~84% of revenue), and the ATE duopoly with Advantest means the curve accrues to Teradyne rather than commoditizing - evidenced by 104% revenue growth and operating margin more than doubling. Main caveat is cyclicality: it rides the curve with high beta in both directions.

balance_sheet.note: Cash and marketable securities of NT$3,518B (~US$111B) against NT$864B (~US$27B) of interest-bearing debt (converted at ~31.6 TWD/USD), a very large net-cash position.

segments.note: 66% of revenue, +20% QoQ; AI/HPC is now two-thirds of the business

segments.note: 22% of revenue, -4% QoQ; seasonally soft

segments.name: IoT / Automotive / DCE & Other
segments.note: Combined ~12% of revenue; automotive +15% QoQ

companies.guidance_note: Q3 2026 guided to $44.6-45.8B revenue (+~12% QoQ) with 65-67% gross margin, and full-year 2026 USD revenue growth raised to 'slightly above 40%'.
companies.execution_note: Multiple consecutive quarters of beats (USD revenue growth of 25-41% YoY each of the last four quarters) with the full-year outlook raised again in July, a clear beat-and-raise pattern.

moat.note: Effective monopoly in leading-edge logic manufacturing (~90%+ of sub-5nm output) with 2nm ramping, ecosystem lock-in via design flows/packaging (CoWoS), and customers (Apple, NVIDIA, AMD) with no comparable alternative.

risks: Taiwan geopolitical/China concentration risk on the vast majority of leading-edge capacity
Margin dilution from overseas fab buildouts, 2nm ramp costs, and TWD appreciation

thesis_fit.note: TSMC is the physical substrate of the compute exponential: every major AI accelerator and leading smartphone SoC is made on its leading-edge nodes, so the cost/performance curve of compute flows directly through its P&L (HPC now 66% of revenue, growing 20% QoQ). The exponential is the core business, not adjacent, and its process monopoly means the value of each node transition accrues to TSMC rather than commoditizing — visible in record 67.7% gross margins. The one structural caveat is geopolitical concentration, not thesis fit.

companies.guidance_note: Guided September 2026 quarter revenue to a step-change $8.1B ±$0.4B (~+52% YoY) with 52% gross margin and 39.5% operating margin, calling 2027 an 'extraordinary' year on AI-driven memory demand.
companies.execution_note: Record revenue and EPS with YoY growth accelerating four quarters running (22% to 30%) capped by a dramatic guidance raise — a clear beat-and-raise pattern.

moat.note: Leader in etch and deposition, the most critical steps for 3D NAND, HBM/advanced DRAM, and gate-all-around, with high switching costs from process-of-record wins and a large installed base — but it operates in a contested oligopoly with Tokyo Electron and Applied rather than a monopoly.

thesis_fit.note: Lam's revenue is directly geared to the steepest part of the compute exponential right now — HBM and 3D NAND scaling for AI, where etch and deposition intensity per wafer keeps rising. The exponential is the core business and Lam's process-of-record positions in critical steps let it capture the curve (record 37%+ operating margins, +30% growth, ~+52% guided). It earns 'high' on all three tests, with the caveat that memory-cycle amplitude makes the ride far more volatile than TSMC or KLA.

companies.name: AppLovin Corporation

margins.trend_note: GAAP operating margin expanded to ~78% from ~76% a year ago as the pure-advertising model (post games divestiture) scales with near-zero incremental cost.

fcf.note: Q2 2026 FCF was $863M vs ~$770M a year ago; the asset-light model converts roughly two-thirds of revenue to free cash flow with negligible capex.

companies.execution_note: Has consistently delivered revenue at or above the high end of guidance for multiple consecutive quarters with sequential margin expansion.

moat.note: Dominant MAX mediation position and the Axon recommendation engine create data-scale network effects and real switching costs in mobile UA, though Meta, Google, Unity and Moloco contest the broader performance-ad market.

risks: Platform/privacy policy changes by Apple and Google could impair targeting data
Competition from Meta/Google/Moloco in performance advertising and unproven durability of e-commerce expansion

thesis_fit.note: AppLovin is one of the cleanest public expressions of the AI/compute curve as the core business: revenue is generated directly by machine-learning ad models (Axon) whose performance improves with more compute and data, the exponential is the product rather than an adjacency, and 50%+ growth at ~78% GAAP operating margins is evidence the curve is currently accruing to the company rather than commoditizing. The main caveat to durability is that it competes with the largest AI companies on earth (Meta, Google), so the moat leg is the weakest of the three.

Its quasi-monopoly in inspection means the curve accrues to KLA (61% gross / 42% operating margins, stable across cycles). Slightly more cyclical than TSMC but all three thesis tests are met.

Cleaner GAAP financials than Synopsys currently, at the cost of a richer valuation.

companies.name: Arm Holdings plc

margins.trend_note: GAAP operating margin compressed to 7.1% from 10.8% a year ago as Arm invests heavily (R&D, SBC, and the new AGI CPU silicon effort), while non-GAAP operating margin expanded ~200bps to 41%.

fcf.note: Company-reported TTM FCF of ~$1.4B with Q1 FCF of ~$0.67-0.71B, up roughly 343% YoY in the quarter on royalty strength and licensing collections — small in dollars but inflecting sharply.

balance_sheet.note: $3.9B cash and short-term investments against ~$0.5B debt — a clean net-cash, asset-light balance sheet.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: $715M; data-center royalties more than doubled YoY, Armv9 and CSS driving higher rates per chip

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: $574M; ACV +13% YoY to $1.73B, AGI CPU demand >$2B across FY27-28

companies.guidance_note: Guided Q2 FY2027 revenue to $1.38B ±$50M (non-GAAP EPS $0.47 ±$0.04) but trimmed FY2027 royalty growth to high-teens from ~20% on double-digit smartphone weakness, with ~30% licensing growth offsetting; separately set a $25B FY2031 revenue target including a new $15B AGI CPU silicon business.
companies.execution_note: Q1 beat estimates on record royalty and licensing, but the FY2027 royalty-growth trim makes the recent pattern beat-on-quarter/soften-on-outlook rather than clean beat-and-raise.

moat.note: The Arm ISA's ecosystem lock-in (nearly all smartphones, fast-growing Neoverse data-center share, decades of software compatibility) creates enormous switching costs; held back from a 5 by RISC-V encroachment, customer litigation history, and the execution risk of moving into silicon in competition with its own licensees.

risks: GAAP profitability is thin (7% operating margin) while opex ramps for the AGI CPU silicon bet, which also risks channel conflict with licensees
Smartphone royalty base (still the largest segment) declining double digits per management
RISC-V as a royalty-free architectural alternative, especially in China
Reported FTC probe and concentrated ownership/related-party dynamics with SoftBank
Valuation-scale expectations embedded in the $25B FY2031 target

thesis_fit.note: Arm is a per-unit royalty on the proliferation of compute itself — every efficiency gain on the compute cost curve expands the addressable unit base, and the mix is shifting toward the steepest part of the curve (data-center royalties doubling YoY, Neoverse past 1.5B cores, Armv9/CSS lifting royalty rates per chip). The exponential is the core business and the ISA ecosystem is a genuine moat, so it meets all three tests. Watch-items that could downgrade the fit: the smartphone base (the legacy majority of royalties) is shrinking, GAAP margins are compressing during the investment phase, and the pivot into selling its own AGI CPU silicon trades the pure toll-booth model for higher-risk, lower-margin revenue.

The duopoly structure means the curve accrues to Synopsys rather than commoditizing it, and Ansys extends this into simulation-driven engineering. Integration debt and GAAP margin noise are transitional, not structural, detractors.

thesis_fit.note: Lilly rides a genuine biology platform curve - iterative peptide/incretin engineering (tirzepatide, retatrutide, oral orforglipron) plus industrial-scale biologics manufacturing - and that platform, not a single legacy drug, is driving 48% growth, which satisfies the first two legs reasonably well. But the business model remains classic patent-cycle pharma rather than a compounding technology curve: the cost/performance improvement of drug discovery is not yet the engine, and post-patent commoditization is the historical norm, so the moat leg is time-limited. Two of three legs: medium.

Two of three criteria met: strong exponential linkage and core-business exposure, weaker moat durability.

Strong franchise, but more of a diversified cyclical on the exponential than a pure toll-taker.

margins.trend_note: Gross margin fell ~3pp YoY (71.8% vs 74.9%) on GPU/AI-inference network buildout, and the headline GAAP operating loss widened to -29.6% because of a restructuring charge — excluding that, underlying GAAP losses (~-8 to -10% in recent quarters) are roughly flat vs a year ago while non-GAAP op margin held at 13.8%.

fcf.note: TTM FCF of ~$337M compares with $288M for FY2025, and H1 2026 FCF of ~$150M was up ~50% vs H1 2025's ~$100M, though Q2's 8% FCF margin dipped on stepped-up AI capex.

balance_sheet.note: $4.16B of cash and investments against ~$3.27B of convertible notes leaves ~$0.9B net cash.

segments.name: Total (no segment disclosure)
segments.note: Cloudflare reports one segment; growth reaccelerated to 36% (fastest in ~3 years) on AI, agentic-web, and platform ('act-as-one') deals, with current RPO up 35% YoY.

bench.guidance_note: Raised FY2026 guidance to $2.864-$2.870B revenue (~33% growth) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.25-$1.26, with Q3 revenue guided to $736-$737M.
bench.execution_note: Beat Q2 estimates and raised the full-year outlook, sending shares up ~17% to record highs, extending a consistent recent pattern of beats with accelerating top-line growth.

moat.note: A genuinely unique global anycast network within ~50ms of most internet users plus the Workers developer ecosystem confer scale and data advantages, but Cloudflare fights hyperscalers, Akamai, and Zscaler across every product line — advantaged but heavily contested.

risks: Persistent GAAP losses and heavy SBC dilution
Hyperscaler competition in edge compute and AI inference
Gross-margin compression from GPU capex, plus a very demanding valuation

thesis_fit.note: Cloudflare is repositioning from CDN/security toward being the connective and inference layer of the agentic internet — Workers AI, AI crawler monetization, and edge GPU deployment tie it increasingly to the compute exponential, and growth reaccelerating to 36% suggests it is landing. But today's revenue base is still majority security/network services where AI is an accelerant rather than the core curve, and its moat, while real (unmatched network footprint), is contested by hyperscalers who own the underlying compute economics. Two of three criteria solidly met; core-exponential purity is the gap.

segments.note: 77 systems in deployment; backlog ~$22.5B anchored by Walmart, plus Walmex/Target/Albertsons; no separate segment YoY disclosed.

bench.execution_note: FQ3 came in at/above its own guidance with adjusted EBITDA of $95M more than doubling YoY, continuing a recent beat streak, but the company has a checkered history (2024 revenue-recognition restatement) and shares often trade off on guidance tone.

moat.note: Proprietary end-to-end warehouse automation with deep Walmart integration and a $22.5B backlog creates real switching costs at existing customers, but the space is contested (Dematic, AutoStore, Ocado, Amazon in-house) and extreme customer concentration caps the rating.

risks: Walmart concentration (majority of revenue and backlog)
Lumpy, deposit-driven cash flow that can reverse (latest quarter FCF negative)
Thin gross margins for a 'tech' multiple; execution/restatement history
Competition from in-house and rival automation platforms

thesis_fit.note: Symbotic scores on two of three exponential-thesis legs: revenue is driven by the robotics/AI-autonomy cost-performance curve, and that curve IS the core business (autonomous warehouse robots replacing manual case-handling). What it lacks is a durable moat that guarantees the curve accrues to Symbotic - the business is dominated by one customer relationship, competitors are numerous and well-funded, and 22% gross margins suggest limited pricing power so far. The 20%+ growth, swing to GAAP profitability, and $22.5B backlog are genuine evidence of the thesis working, but concentration risk keeps it at medium.

Where it falls short of 'high' is moat durability: the launch cost curve is being driven hardest by SpaceX, and much of Rocket Lab's advantage (execution, cadence, integration) is operational rather than structural, so it is not certain the curve accrues to RKLB rather than to its far larger competitor. Strong balance sheet and beat-and-raise execution derisk the path, but persistent cash burn means the model is not yet self-funding.

The exciting part, Commercial Operations up 72% on the AI-power-driven nuclear renaissance plus SMR/TRISO/medical-isotope optionality, is real but is demand exposure to someone else's exponential (compute) rather than a compounding curve in BWXT's own product. Only one of the three exponential-thesis legs (moat) is clearly satisfied, so it fits as a high-quality compounder rather than an exponential-age pure play.

But the exponential is the customer, not the product - Vistra sells commodity electrons, its fleet is not on a technology learning curve (gas/nuclear/coal, with renewables a minority), and its advantage is asset scarcity plus interconnection queues rather than a compounding technology moat. Two-of-three at best: strong demand-side exposure to the exponential and a defensible-for-now asset position, but the core business is not itself exponential technology.

segments.note: Product-level splits not verified from the summary release; company cited oral Wegovy exceeding 265,000 weekly US prescriptions and >5M scripts since launch, with guidance raised on 'increased expectations for GLP-1 product sales'.

thesis_fit.note: Novo sits on the same GLP-1 biology wave as Lilly, but the evidence no longer supports the curve accruing to the company: reported sales grew only ~2% in DKK in the latest quarter, full-year adjusted guidance is for a decline, and the franchise is losing the innovation race to Lilly while facing compounding/generic erosion. The underlying technology (peptide engineering, oral delivery) is real, but it is a single maturing franchise rather than a compounding platform, and the moat leg is failing - at most one of the three thesis legs holds today.
